email.body1:
Max, saw BLAZE rebrand and launch BLAZE Labs to lean into AI-powered cannabis retail.

As the product expands, the real revops bottleneck is rarely the data, it is the latency between a signal firing and a touch going out, so in-market dispensaries cool before a rep reaches them. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for BLAZE off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Max, quick follow-up for BLAZE.

Most revops teams can surface intent faster than the team can act on it, so signal-to-touch latency quietly caps conversion no matter how clean the data is. The measurable win is compressing that lag without adding reps to absorb the new product volume.

I put together a teardown of a signals-to-outbound motion, three things I would change to lift response rates 50 to 70 percent. Want to grab 15 minutes and I will walk you through it?
email.body3:
Max, last bit of proof for BLAZE.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how BLAZE's reply rate likely compares to other vertical-SaaS startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Max, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If compressing signal-to-action latency without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. A rebrand and a new product line is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a signals-driven motion? I will tailor it to BLAZE either way.
